title: Counted simulation of a source run
statement: Let $M$ and $N$ be multi-tape Turing machines, respectively with $k$ and $k+1$ work tapes, and let $\mathrm{emb}$ and $\mathrm{ret}$ be state maps for the host simulation. Suppose that, for every source state, overflow flag, input symbol, and tuple of work-tape symbols, the host transition from the embedded state is the prescribed emission-counting transform of the source transition, using the successor-indexed work tapes. For any finite Boolean words $w,s$, source configuration $c$ over empty input, and time $t$, if the source run from $c$ is not halted at any time $j<t$, then the host run from the embedded configuration of $c$ at time $t$ equals the embedded configuration of the source run at time $t$.
hypotheses_covered: Transition agreement for every state, overflow flag, input symbol, and work-tape tuple
The source run is unhalted at every time $j<t$
replaced:
Suppose the host machine's transitions on embedded states agree with the
emission-counting transform of the source machine's transitions, and the
source, started from a configuration $c$ over the empty input, does not halt
before time $t$. Then $t$ steps of the host from the embedding of $c$ land
exactly on the embedding of the source configuration after $t$ steps; the
host's physical output stays empty throughout.
